title: FA to canvass England players in World Cup review
description: The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.
fullText:
The Football Association's review into England's World Cup campaign will canvass the opinions of players involved in the tournament.

English football's governing body has started the post-tournament review they conduct after every major international competition. The FA says the review is the standard process it undertakes after all tournaments.

Head coach Thomas Tuchel and members of his backroom team were at St George's Park last week where they were involved in unpacking their performance in north America with a wider report into the team's World Cup campaign to be delivered at a later date.

And it is understood members of Tuchel's squad will be spoken to, and their feedback taken into account, as part of the review process.

The players' involvement in the review provides an interesting dynamic given the emerging sense from members of the World Cup squad that Tuchel's substitutions and tactical approach contributed to their semi-final loss to Argentina - despite taking a 1-0 lead through Anthony Gordon.

BBC Sport revealed in the 24 hours after that defeat that at least three senior players privately expressed misgivings about Tuchel's approach in the closing stages of the game.

There was a widely held view that Tuchel's changes and tactical set-up were too defensive late on as they conceded two late goals to lose 2-1.

The ongoing review will also look into the impact of the team's permanent Kansas City base during the tournament.

After every game, they returned to Kansas City - and the effects of the travelling will be analysed.

England went on to defeat France in the bronze medal match to record their best World Cup finish since lifting the trophy in 1966.

With that in mind, key figures at the FA view the tournament as a success and the organisation has backed Tuchel before the Euro 2028 qualifying campaign.

England will play their first game since the World Cup in the Nations League against Spain on 26 September. They will also face two matches in the tournament against the Czech Republic, either side of playing Croatia, during the next international window.

title: How 'unique' Bellingham is thriving in Mourinho's system
description: Jude Bellingham looks fit and ready to build on his World Cup form as he aims to rediscover his best at Real Madrid under Jose Mourinho.
fullText:
Jude Bellingham has started the new season looking like a player with something to prove.

The 23-year-old's two goals and three assists have helped Real Madrid to an impressive start under new boss Jose Mourinho, with three wins from as many games.

Bellingham's performances, and the freedom he has been given in his new role, has attracted a lot of attention.

Bellingham's last two campaigns were less consistent, with his displays and attacking influence affected not only by a deeper role, but by recurring injuries. He had a long-standing shoulder problem that required surgery in 2025 and a hamstring issue that kept him out for 10 matches in 2026.

Now, however, he appears to be at peak fitness, ready to build on his impressive World Cup form for England and showcase the full extent of his talent.

Since returning this summer to take charge of the club for a second spell, Mourinho has made an important adjustment in reducing the defensive workload that previously meant Bellingham had to cover huge areas of the pitch.

"We've organised the team differently," he said after Real Madrid's 4-0 La Liga win over Malaga.

"Bellingham sometimes defended like a second left-back last season. I told him I do not want to see that anymore. I made a deal with him."

The Portuguese manager has used Bellingham primarily as a number 10 in a 4-2-3-1 system, operating behind French striker Kylian Mbappe and with the freedom to move across the attacking line.

That gives the England midfielder a clearer role. Rather than constantly moving between midfield, defence and attack, he can spend more time in the areas where he is most dangerous.

"For me, this is his position, with his connection with the forwards, he can score goals," added Mourinho.

"He has to play close to the goal. Playing at number six or number eight, we're losing his closeness to the goal. I like this Jude."

It has meant Bellingham can receive the ball between the lines, carry it forward, combine with the forwards and make late runs into the penalty area.

Just as importantly, he is being given greater freedom to decide when to move.

Bellingham has explained the difference himself in an interview with Real Madrid TV.

"I feel more free to decide when to drop back, when to stay up or when to get into the box," he said. "I think this is the best position for me."

Mourinho still expects him to press and recover possession, but the difference is where that work begins.

Instead of dropping deep towards his own penalty area, Bellingham can now use his energy to press opponents higher up the pitch.

When Madrid win the ball, he is already closer to the forwards. That allows him to connect midfield with attack and provide another player who can combine with Mbappe and Vinicius Jr.

It also explains why Mourinho has been keen to stress Madrid's attacking players must work together rather than operate as individuals.

"The team dynamic is about 11, not 2+9," he said.

The midfielder also described working with Mourinho as a "dream", having previously only met the former Chelsea, Manchester United and Tottenham manager once before his appointment.

There is clearly an early understanding and respect between the two.

Mourinho has repeatedly spoken about Bellingham's importance to his plans, describing him as a "unique and super important player" with qualities that include physical, mental and tactical.

He also suggested Bellingham should be one of the players in the running for the Ballon d'Or.

"He is a unique kind of player and extremely important for the team," said Mourinho.

"His mental strength, tactical ability, the way he recovers the ball, the way he pressures, the way he plays up front, I am very happy."

For Mourinho, that versatility is part of what makes Bellingham so valuable. He can press, recover possession, score, contribute in the air and drive the team forward.

The Real boss has also pointed to Thomas Tuchel's use of Bellingham at the World Cup as an example of how to get the best out of him.

Bellingham was one of England's standout players, finishing with seven goals and an assist in his eight appearances, and his attacking qualities were allowed to flourish.

That experience also appears to have given the player a confidence boost, particularly as he rejoined Madrid later than most of his team-mates and had less time to prepare for the new campaign.

Although Real's three league wins - scoring 10 goals and conceding two - are only a small sample, and the demands will increase as the season progresses amid Champions League football, the early signs are very positive.

For Bellingham, whose huge strength has always been his ability to affect almost every part of a game, Mourinho's system has given him more control over where that influence is used.

After a difficult couple of seasons following the high standards he set in his first year, the England midfielder is enjoying his football again.

"I'm having a lot of fun, I'm really enjoying my football, and that's why I'm performing well," he told club media.

If he continues in this vein with Mourinho's continued support, it could turn out to be his best season yet.

fullText:
The FIBA World Cup tips off on Friday with a 16-team field. More than 50 WNBA players, who are on a two-week break from the league, will take part in the competition as the United States seeks its fifth consecutive title, and 15 other federations attempt to dethrone the champs.

Here's what to know as play begins:

It's hard to overstate the Americans' dominance in international competition. Since the creation of the WNBA, Team USA is undefeated in the Olympics — only three wins have come by single digits since 1996 — and it has lost only once in the world championships, which led to a third-place finish in 2006. The Americans have cleaned up at the four world championships since, with double-figure victories in every game but one during that stretch.

Even without A'ja Wilson on this year's roster, Team USA still has the best individual player in the tournament (whether you consider that to be Breanna Stewart, Caitlin Clark, Napheesa Collier or someone else, it's an American) and the best collection of talent. It would be a considerable upset for the Americans to be beaten. Four of Team USA's closest contests during the last 20 years, including the one loss, came to Russia, but that program has fallen off. Since its decline, no true basketball rival has emerged for the United States.

USA Basketball heavily values international tournaments, from the youth level onward. It's why the WNBA, which is the world's premier basketball league, would take a break right before the postseason to accommodate the World Cup and why the best players in this league are eschewing a break of their own to compete. Success on the global stage matters.

For all of the skill Team USA brings to the table, it lost a lot of experience when Wilson (Las Vegas Aces) and Kelsey Plum (Phoenix Mercury) opted out of the tournament due to injuries. The pair have each competed in two Olympics and two World Cups, and Wilson has been the Americans' leading scorer at the last three major international competitions.

Without that duo, Team USA is left with three players with World Cup experience; Breanna Stewart is suiting up for the fourth time, while Chelsea Gray and Kahleah Copper both were on the 2022 roster. Only five players have represented the U.S. in five-on-five at a senior tournament (Rhyne Howard played 3×3 at the last Olympics). The team is so green that four players haven't even appeared in a WNBA playoff game.

Even the coaching staff is a little inexperienced at the international level. Duke coach Kara Lawson has come up through USA Basketball. She coached the inaugural 3×3 team in Tokyo, was an assistant during the last cycle under Cheryl Reeve and won the AmeriCup in 2025 with a roster of college players. But this is the first rodeo for the assistants: Indiana Fever coach Stephanie White, Phoenix coach Nate Tibbetts and Golden State Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase. It will be interesting to see how these coaches respond to game pressure; none has been the head coach of a WNBA or NCAA champion.

During the qualifying tournament, the U.S. tended to start its veterans even though the minutes were relatively evenly distributed. Although Clark started one game, she played enough to earn MVP of the event. Lawson is expected to pick a more experienced starting five — something that includes Stewart, Gray and Copper plus one more guard and a center.

This is an opportunity for Stewart to assert herself as a leader. She has more international experience than just about all of her teammates combined, and she was the MVP of this tournament in 2018. Stewart and Wilson have been the co-stewards of this era of USA Basketball, but the New York Liberty superstar is the only one in Berlin.

Australia has been the most consistently competitive team in international competitions over the past two decades, and it finished third in the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Olympics. The Opals have eight WNBA players, six of whom are currently meaningful rotation players: Alanna Smith (Dallas Wings), Rebecca Allen (Liberty), Ezi Magbegor (Seattle Storm), Jade Melbourne (Storm), Isobel Borlase (Atlanta Dream) and Stephanie Talbot (Aces). What Australia is missing is a singular offensive engine; it's unclear how the Opals can manufacture quality offense in the half court, even if their defensive upside is as good as anyone in the tournament.

Belgium has been the class of the European teams, winners of the last two EuroBasket competitions. Forward Emma Meesseman, the 2019 WNBA Finals MVP who has played only two full WNBA seasons since, always brings it for her national team. Her skill in the post as a passing hub and a scorer is near-unmatched, and she is flanked by two dynamic guards in Julie Allemand (Toronto Tempo) and Julie Vanloo, who are willing creators and attackers.

Mike Thibault is a veteran coach (the second-winningest in WNBA history) who spent time with Meesseman on the Washington Mystics and has been an assistant at the Olympics. The Belgians have something of an it factor, too — they won the 2025 European championship in regulation despite trailing Spain by 12 with 2:42 to play.

One caveat to Belgium's 2025 victory was that the French essentially punted on the tournament. Gabby Williams, Marine Johannès and Dominique Malonga all stayed with their WNBA teams instead of reporting. The last time France had a full roster was at the Paris Olympics 2024, when the home team was one foot away from taking Team USA to overtime in the gold-medal game.

France has an impressive collection of perimeter talent. Among Williams (Valkyries), Carla Leite (Portland Fire) and Pauline Astier (Liberty), several guards can blow by their initial defender and break down a defense. Leite is one week removed from giving Angel Reese and Howard fits in Atlanta, while Astier has tormented the Fever duo of Clark and Aliyah Boston. This is a guard group that will demand that the U.S. defend on a string, which is a tricky thing for a 12-player roster that hasn't ever played together. They are mostly good defenders, too. A backcourt of Williams and Leïla Lacan can cause discomfort for even the American stars.

The French have great spacing throughout their lineup. Johannès and Janelle Salaün (Valkyries) are some of the most willing shooters in the world, and their unorthodox shot releases keep good defense from deterring them. Salaün relishes a contest on her 3-pointer and shoots better with a defender in her face.

France isn't as imposing in the frontcourt, though Salaün and Malonga are a devastating starting combo with the former's shooting and the latter's rim-running. Malonga is also one of the better paint protectors in the entire tournament. Team USA will need to have success from beyond the arc to break France's defense.

Nigeria has quietly given Team USA trouble in recent competitions. It lost by nine to the Americans in the 2020 Olympics group stage and by 14 in the quarterfinals of the 2024 Olympics. Rena Wakama, a current Unrivaled head coach and Chicago Sky assistant, has done a fantastic job establishing a team culture for Nigeria. The group moves the ball well, plays hard and uses its athleticism effectively.

China is the biggest team in the tournament, though it took a sizable hit when 6-foot-7 Li Yueru (Wings) was ruled out due to passport issues. Nevertheless, in addition to 6-11 Han Xu (Liberty), keep an eye on 7-3 Zhang Ziyu. The 19-year-old center is eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft and could improve her stock with a strong showing in Berlin. Unfortunately, the less said about China's guards, the better; their main job is to get the ball past half court without turning it over and then feed the bigs.

Spain has the most active WNBA players (five) among remaining teams, including Storm rookie Awa Fam. An especially intriguing player to watch is Iyana Martín, the Fire's first-round pick, who will be coming stateside next season. Martín has a phenomenal track record at junior competitions, including winning MVP of the 2023 U-19 World Cup when Spain lost in the finals' overtime to the U.S. That group is all grown up, and this is now Martín's first foray at the senior level, where she has just the right amount of flair and playmaking verve to complement the rock-solid production of Megan DiLeo (Fire) in the paint.

Every Team USA game will be on TNT or truTV, and the entire tournament can be streamed on HBO Max.

title: BCCI meeting decoded: Devajit Saikia reveals big plans for injuries, SENA tours and 2027 World Cup
description: The BCCI is set to enhance its overseas performance strategy while tackling player injuries. They aim to craft a robust plan in preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup, which will require adjustments in the Future Tours Programme to prioritise player rest. Recent defeats in white-ball matches against England and Ireland were carefully analysed, and insight was gathered from captains and the head coach regarding fitness protocols.
fullText:
NEW DELHI: The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) has drawn up a roadmap to address India's recent overseas setbacks, mounting player injuries and preparations for the 2027 ODI World Cup, with secretary Devajit Saikia revealing details of Thursday's high-level review meeting in Mumbai.

The meeting, attended by head coach Gautam Gambhir, Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill, T20I captain Shreyas Iyer and Centre of Excellence director VVS Laxman, reviewed India's recent tours of Ireland and England as well as the team's preparations for the next phase of the international calendar.

Chief selector Ajit Agarkar was absent, but Saikia said there was no controversy behind his non-participation and insisted no discussion took place about his future.

Saikia strongly rejected suggestions of a communication gap between the team management and the Centre of Excellence, particularly after several high-profile injury setbacks.

"Everybody is on the same page. BCCI is working in a very well like a well oiled engine," Saikia told reporters.

"There is proper coordination amongst all the wings of BCCI, whether it is women's teams committees or their technical staff or their coaches, vis-a-vis the COE, vis-a-vis the Indian men's team's coaching staff and the head coach. There is no difficulty in the coordination, everything is moving in the right direction."

However, he admitted that the frequency of injuries remains a major concern and said the board intends to address it through changes to the next Future Tours Programme (FTP).

"The only challenge which we are facing is that there are too many matches in the year and that is why in the next FTP we will do certain things, we will take certain measures."

The proposed changes will particularly affect preparation for tours to SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.

"We have instructed our FTP persons who will be meeting very soon in various international forums that our FTP should be in such a way it should be scheduled that there is proper rest for the players as well as some kind of acclimatisation or some kind of friendly matches before any major series in SENA countries," Saikia said.

The comments come after India suffered a difficult run in overseas white-ball cricket, losing 0-2 to Ireland in the T20Is before a 1-4 defeat to England in the five-match series. India also lost the ODI series in England 1-2.

Saikia acknowledged India's shortcomings and said the review meeting focused on understanding why the team had struggled.

"We discussed (about) our team performed in England and Ireland and also about what we are going to do about the next one year. The road map has been prepared and we will be doing some exercises so that we have a very good performance in 2027 (ODI) World Cup," he said.

"Yes, we did not do well. We lost matches in Ireland and England, so we wanted to know what the reasons were. We have to do certain soul searching about that, and in future, what we will be doing before going to any of the SENA countries, we have chalked out some strategy on that."

The board also revisited its Return to Play protocols, with feedback sought directly from Gill, Iyer and Gambhir.

"Today's discussion was totally general in nature, what policy and protocols we have to maintain regarding maintaining the fitness level of every player -- not any individual -- and what is best interest of the team, we have considered that only," Saikia said.

"We have taken the feedback from the captains and the head coach who are the right persons to give us the information, so that we chalk up a proper strategy to avoid all this kind of unwanted situations during matches."

Saikia also pushed back against renewed speculation surrounding Rohit Sharma's ODI future and his prospects of playing at the 2027 World Cup.

"He is playing superbly in all the matches. So, what more do you want? In the last match, he scored 138 runs. So, why there is a speculation? So, I don't want to give fodder to the speculations," Saikia said.

Rohit had scored a century at Lord's in his last ODI appearance, intensifying the debate over whether he would continue until the 2027 World Cup.

Saikia also explained why Agarkar was absent from the meeting.

"Today he (Agarkar) was out of station, so he could not be a part of the meeting. Because this meeting was called at very short notice and our head of the selection committee, Ajit Agarkar, was not in town, he could not join it, and he was in such an area that he could not join online also, despite our best efforts," he said.

"There was no such discussion on this in today's meeting. I do not comment on new rumours. We did not have any such discussions, nor did we have such intentions."

He further ruled out any discussion about appointing a new director of cricket.

"There was no discussion on the selection committee. Our whole focus was on performances in England and Ireland, as well as the recent Test series in Sri Lanka and what we are going to do in the upcoming series before the ODI World Cup, which is our ultimate goal," Saikia said.

The vacant Head of Sports Science and Medicine position at the CoE was another issue addressed by Saikia, who insisted it had not affected the centre's functioning.

"I would like to reiterate once more that the vacant position of the head of the sports science is not a deterrent of our activities in COE," he said.

"(Filling) that post is required, but that is a very high level post, and for that, a proper qualified person should be positioned. We have about 16 persons in place to maintain the fitness level or the rehab facilities."

"To supervise that one important person is required, and for that he must be qualified up to a different level. That kind of person is very less in number in India, as well as in the whole world.

"We are trying to find out that kind of a person at the earliest possible time but without him also it is running in the right manner," Saikia added.

The meeting, therefore, ended without any major immediate personnel changes, but with the BCCI setting out a broader plan: reduce the burden of an overcrowded calendar, improve overseas preparation, strengthen injury management and build towards the 2027 World Cup.

title: Fifa accuses Uefa of 'smear campaign' against Infantino
description: The governing bodies have traded blows since Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.
fullText:
Fifa has accused Uefa of a "smear campaign against it and its leadership" in a challenge to litigation over president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

Last week European football's governing body filed legal papers in the US requesting disclosure of evidence and documents from Fifa as part of potential criminal claims in Switzerland.

In a dramatic escalation of the controversy, Uefa accused Infantino of "criminal mismanagement" and "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by [him] for his own benefit" over the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme.

However, world governing body Fifa has now responded with court filings lodged in the US - and seen by the BBC - requesting that permission for access to documents be deferred, or opposed by the end of the month.

Fifa claims Uefa's argument "suffers from a fundamental defect" and "legal deficiencies".

"Uefa seeks discovery in aid of a foreign criminal proceeding that does not exist and that Uefa admittedly lacks the authority to initiate. Despite that threshold problem, Uefa asks this court to authorise sweeping discovery about the FFE."

It said it had "made clear" that the creation of FFE was "only a proposal", adding that it could have only proceeded on the condition that the majority of member associations supported it and "the relevant approvals of the Fifa Council".

"Rather than participate in that democratic process, Uefa issued a press release - the beginning of a weeks-long smear campaign against Fifa and its leadership," it wrote in the court filing.

Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?

Kushner states regret over World Cup sell-off plan

Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino

It also claimed that Uefa's "economic motivation" was to prevent smaller countries from having the "financial strength to compete with the European elite".

"If soccer is strengthened in the developing world, global competition increases, which ultimately reduces Uefa's market power and provides more competition for its flagship tournaments," Fifa said.

"By raising funds to allow some of Fifa's smaller member associations to better develop soccer, FFE would lead to more players from those nations choosing to represent their countries of origin and playing in their home leagues rather than playing abroad."

Uefa has declined to comment, although BBC Sport has been told insiders believe that if Fifa has nothing to hide, it should disclose the documents and speed up the legal process. It has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down from three confederations.

Uefa has also asked a court in New York to approve a legal document ordering testimony and documents from venture capitalist Joshua Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, who was set to be the lead investor in FFE, and his company Thrive Eternal.

Thrive had held talks with Infantino about heading up a $4.2bn (£3.1bn) investment in 20% of a new Fifa commercial subsidiary, before the idea was abandoned days after it was revealed in July amid a huge backlash.

At the time, Fifa claimed FFE would have increased the funding distributed to each national association for the 2027-2030 cycle from £5.9m to £14.7m.

On Sunday, Kushner expressed regret over FFE, saying: "While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to… had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

Uefa has also asked for the disclosure of documents from American financier Greg Maffei, who was a key adviser on the deal.

While Uefa says neither Kushner nor Maffei are anticipated defendants in any legal proceedings, it claims the pair first discussed the FFE concept in July 2025 and that Infantino had "been discussing the underlying concept with Kushner for nearly a year before the terms sheet was ultimately signed".

Its lawyers also argue the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at about £15bn, which it says is "a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". Uefa claims Infantino failed to consult Fifa's hierarchy over the plan.

title: Who will USA play in 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup group phase? Full schedule
description: Team USA seeks a fifth straight gold medal with a roster featuring nine first-time players and veteran Breanna Stewart.
fullText:
The U.S. women's national basketball team hasn't lost a FIBA World Cup game since September 2006, a dominant stretch that has resulted in four consecutive World Cup gold medals. The Americans are vying for their fifth consecutive gold in Berlin, Germany, with a team mix of veteran and newbies.

Team USA is headlined by veteran Breanna Stewart, a three-time Olympic gold medalist and three-time World Cup gold medalist that'll join Sue Bird (5) and Diana Taurasi (4) as the only American women to appear in at least four World Cups. Aside from Stewart, only Kahleah Copper and Chelsea Gray have previously competed in red, white and blue at the World Cup. Everyone else is a newcomer.

"We have nine first-time players in the World Cup, so only three of our players have ever played in a World Cup before," Team USA head coach Kara Lawson said on Tuesday, Sept. 1. "There's a lot of newness to our roster... What is my message to the young players? Be yourself. Your play and your confidence is what brought you here."

Aliyah Boston, Paige Bueckers, Caitlin Clark, Napheesa Collier, Rhyne Howard, Angel Reese, Jackie Young, Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron are set to make their FIBA World Cup debuts. Here's who the USA will face in 2026 FIBA women's World Cup group phase:

The U.S. women's national team is in Group D at the 2026 FIBA World Cup alongside China, Italy, Czechia.

Group A: Germany, Spain, Japan, Mali

Group B: France, Nigeria, Korea, Hungary

Group C: Australia, Belgium, Puerto Rico, Turkey

Group D: USA, China, Italy, Czechia

TNT has the exclusive U.S. English-language rights. All 36 games stream on HBOMax. Seventeen of those games air on TNT and truTV, including every U.S. game.

Friday, Sept. 4: USA vs. China | TNT, truTV, HBO Max (8 a.m. ET)

Sunday, Sept. 6: USA vs. Italy | TNT, HBO Max (2:30 p.m. ET)

Monday, Sept. 7: USA vs. Czechia | TNT, HBO Max (2:30 p.m. ET)

The winner of each group will automatically advance to the quarterfinals on Thursday, Sept. 10 (TNT, truTV). The second- and third-place finishers of each group will play in the Playoff Qualification Round on Tuesday, Sept. 8 (truTV) to determine the final four quarterfinal spots. The semifinals will be held on Saturday, Sept. 12 (TBS, truTV), followed by the third-place game and final on Sunday, Sept. 13 (TNT, truTV).

title: Queiroz returns as Ghana manager two months after stepping down
description: Carlos Queiroz is reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team, two months after he appeared to step down following their exit from the World Cup.
fullText:
Carlos Queiroz has been reappointed as head coach of Ghana's men's national team.

The 73-year-old, who had two spells as assistant manager at Manchester United under Sir Alex Ferguson, took charge of the Black Stars in April and led the side to the last 32 at this year's Fifa World Cup, where they were beaten 1-0 by Colombia.

Queiroz appeared to announce his own departure on social media shortly after that defeat, but the Ghana Football Association (GFA) has decided to re-engage him for another spell in charge following internal discussions.

The GFA has not announced the length of his new deal but said he will prepare the team for "a successful new phase on the international stage".

"The GFA believes Queiroz's extensive international experience, technical expertise and knowledge of the Black Stars position him strongly to lead the team into this next chapter," a statement added.

Queiroz has previously led Iran, Portugal and Egypt at major tournaments and has had stints in charge of South Africa, Colombia and Qatar.

Further details on his mandate will be announced by the GFA in due course.

Queiroz will begin his second spell in charge of the West Africans with qualifiers for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations, which begin later this month.

The Black Stars are yet to announce the dates and venues for their first two fixtures in Group C, where they have been drawn alongside Ivory Coast, The Gambia and Somalia.

title: What awaits USWNT during 2027 Women’s World Cup qualification
description: The USWNT doesn’t need to do much to qualify, but they should not take it for granted.
fullText:
The 2027 Women's World Cup is less than 11 months away as 32 teams will gather in Brazil for the tournament. For the United States women's national team, it's a chance to try and get back to being world champions after their title was snatched in 2023 after holding it for eight years.

Now that the Women's World Cup match schedule has been released, all attention is starting to shift towards qualification. But, what does the USWNT need to do to qualify for the Women's World Cup?

We take a look at the road to the 2027 Women's World Cup and what awaits the USWNT this fall.

The October international window is the final round of friendlies before the qualification tournament. The USWNT, ranked second in the FIFA world rankings, plays a pair of friendlies against Spain, the top ranked team and defending Women's World Cup champions. It's not only a huge pair of matches between the top two ranked teams in the world, but also a barometer test.

Then, the November-December international window is when the 2026 Concacaf W Championship will take place in Texas. The tournament serves as both Women's World Cup qualifying and qualification for the 2028 Olympics. Eight teams (USA, Canada, Mexico, Jamaica, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Haiti, and Panama) will compete in a single elimination tournament over the course of nine days in Mansfield, TX and Houston.

The quarterfinal round is the most important for the USWNT in terms of World Cup qualifying. Should they win their quarterfinal match against El Salvador on Nov. 27, the opening match of the tournament, they will qualify directly for the 2027 Women's World Cup. The four quarterfinal winners earn Concacaf's direct bids to the tournament in Brazil.

Should the unexpected happen and the USWNT loses to El Salvador, they would still have a chance to qualify via a series of playoffs. The four quarterfinal losers will move to the play-in round, as Concacaf has two slots in the FIFA Women's World Cup playoffs in February. To fill those slots, the four quarterfinal losers will play, with the winners moving onto the FIFA playoff. For the USWNT, should they be in the play-in round, they would face the loser of the Jamaica-Costa Rica quarterfinal.

The rest of the 2026 Concacaf W Championship, in addition to crowning the region's champion, will be used for Olympic qualifying. Since the 2028 Olympics will be hosted in Los Angeles, the USWNT has an automatic spot as hosts. The top three teams not named the United States at the Concacaf W Championship will also book their place in the 2028 Olympics.

For the USWNT, winning one match to directly qualify for the Women's World Cup may seem like an easy thing, but the players cannot take it for granted. The team doesn't have to look back that far to see what happens when there's a slip-up in the qualification. In 2010, after losing to Mexico in the semifinals of the Concacaf W Championship, the USWNT needed a FIFA playoff win over Italy to qualify for the 2011 Women's World Cup.

Head coach Emma Hayes wants to leave no doubt and qualify directly this time around so attention can turn towards World Cup preparation. After the October friendlies against Spain are complete, the USWNT will focus on winning the Concacaf W Championship and booking tickets to Brazil in the process.

title: ‘Should Never Play for Team US Again’ – WNBA World Reacts As USA Head Coach Shrugs Off A’ja Wilson Absence Question

fullText:
Team USA released its roster and schedule for the 2026 FIBA Women's World Cup on Tuesday, and although most of the women were expected to be on the roster, there were a few moves (or non-moves) that drew questions.
Although the likes of Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers, and Angel Reese will be playing for Team USA, it came as a surprise to many that Team USA will be without Las Vegas Aces' star A'Ja Wilson.

Wilson, the number one overall pick of the 2018 draft, is having another outstanding season, averaging 26.0 points, 9.4 rebounds, 3.2 assists, 2.0 blocks, and 1.4 steals in 32.0 minutes per game.

Wilson is shooting 52.3% from the field and 39.8% from three. Wilson is a three-time WNBA champion, two-time Finals MVP, eight-time All-Star, three-time Defensive Player of the Year, and four-time MVP.

Simply put, she is one of, if not the, best player in the WNBA right now, so it's clear why her absence has drawn so many questions.

Another mainstay, Kelsey Plum of the Phoenix Mercury, also won't be playing due to injury. Team USA head coach Kara Lawson gave her reaction to the news.

"Both of them [Kelsey Plum included] obviously have been great players for us, and I'll miss being around them, but ultimately, we've kind of moved on…" Lawson said. "We don't have time to be worried about who's not here. We've got to really focus on ourselves."

That's the only kind of mindset that Lawson can have at this time. Of course, with an incredible roster still miles more talented and deeper than any other country, it's probably easy to get over a couple of key players missing the tournament.

Lawson addressed several issues but said she had not spoken with A'ja Wilson about her decision not to play in the World Cup. Sue Bird apparently handled that.

"I didn't have any conversation with A'ja (Wilson)," Lawson said.

They wrote: "Damn! Kara Lawson seems upset about A'ja Wilson quitting on her team so late!"

Whether it's quitting on the team is debatable, but you can see why Lawson may be upset. Leena points out that no one really knows why Wilson isn't playing.

"So is Aja sick or injured? I'm so confused on how nobody from Team USA knows what's going on with her?"they asked. It's an interesting question, and the uncertainty will only lead to more questions and speculation.

Shraddha thinks Wilson should have been more 'professional.' "That sounds bad," they said. "A'ja was not professional about it at all."

All in all, this does not seem like it was handled well on Wilson's part, and that's only going to add fuel to the fan's fire.

title: Kushner states regret over World Cup sell-off plan
description: Venture capitalist Joshua Kushner says he would not have got involved in Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup if he had known how the football world reacted.
fullText:
Venture capitalist Joshua Kushner, who was set to be the lead investor in Fifa president Gianni Infantino's scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup, says he now regrets joining the proposal.

In his first public comments since the now-shelved Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme sparked a major crisis for the governing body, Kushner said: "Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved".

The brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Kushner added he had "failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football".

However, he also defended the proposal, saying, "we stand behind the motivations of FFE", and that its intention "was to direct more capital and equity equally" among Fifa's 211 member associations.

Thrive Eternal, a firm founded by Kushner, had held talks with Infantino about heading up a $4.2bn (£3.1bn) investment in 20% of a new Fifa commercial subsidiary, before the idea was abandoned days after it was revealed in July amid a huge backlash.

Division, drama and power - what next for Infantino and Uefa?

Is football AI-proof? Why tech investors wanted a slice of the World Cup

Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino

Kushner's comments come just days after Uefa asked a court in New York to approve subpoenas for testimony and documents from both the American billionaire and Thrive as it considers lodging a criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland.

European football's governing body Uefa has led the rebellion against the Fifa president, who is facing calls to stand down.

In a statement, Kushner said: "Money in football has historically been concentrated amongst a small group of countries.

"The idea behind FFE was to direct more capital and equity equally amongst all 211 member countries, providing significantly more investment to underdeveloped nations to nurture local talent, support grassroots football, enhance the fan experience, and ultimately grow the global game everywhere.

"It was an idea that every member association would vote on, not an obligation or determination.

"While we stand behind the motivations of FFE, we failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football, and the lengths some would go to. Thrive has a long track record of being a partner to all constituents. Had we known what this would devolve into, we would not have gotten involved."

In late July, shortly before scrapping the plan, Fifa said, "Thrive Eternal...is expected to lead the proposed investor group for FFE", claiming it would have seen the funding distributed to each national association for the 2027-2030 cycle increase from £5.9m to £14.7m.

As well as Kushner, Uefa has asked for the disclosure of documents from two Fifa businesses in the US and American financier Greg Maffei, who was a key adviser on the deal.

While Uefa says neither Kushner nor Maffei are anticipated defendants in any legal proceedings, it claims the pair first discussed the FFE concept in July 2025 and that Infantino had "been discussing the underlying concept with Kushner for nearly a year before the terms sheet was ultimately signed."

Its lawyers also argue the World Cup was deliberately undervalued at around £15bn, which it says is "a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer". It claims Infantino failed to consult Fifa's hierarchy over the plan.

Kushner has recently agreed a deal to buy basketball's Los Angeles Lakers for a record $12.5bn (£9.3bn).

title: Three-week international break a concern - Mourinho
description: Jose Mourinho says the three-week international break is a “concern” for Real Madrid, with several key players facing a demanding schedule after the World Cup.
fullText:
Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho has raised concerns about the impact of September's three-week international break, highlighting the amount of time his players will be away from their club.

"The international break does concern me," Mourinho said. "It's a lot of time."

Speaking before Sunday's home La Liga match against Malaga (16:00 BST), Mourinho said he was mostly troubled by players linking up with their nations who then do not get game time.

"Players who will join their national teams to play don't worry me as much. It's the ones who join the national teams and are not really involved that concern me," he said.

"We'll see how we can go about this and work with the rest of the players. But not having players at my disposal for three weeks is a difficult situation."

The first international break of the 2026-27 men's football season next month will last a week longer than usual, with the traditional October break now scrapped.

In recent years, Fifa has used five primary international breaks during the season, in March, June, September, October and November.

But instead of separate breaks in September and October, there will now be a three-week gap for international fixtures across late September and early October, when countries will play four international matches instead of two. The existing international breaks in November, March and June will remain.

A number of reasons are behind the change, including the 2026 World Cup final being played on 19 July, the latest date for a summer World Cup since 1966. Player welfare and travel considerations were also taken into account when the changes were made.

"I totally respect the players' decisions and I don't want to dramatise too much, but very often they pick up injuries during those breaks and right after returning from an international break," Mourinho explained.

"So it does worry me, but this is the way these things are and we can't do much about it."

The Portuguese has already spoken at length about the World Cup players in his Real Madrid squad, including Jude Bellingham, Marc Cucurella and Kylian Mbappe, who have had a demanding summer.

He said the club are working to manage their workload to reduce the risk of injury.

In his pre-match media conference, Mourinho was also full of praise for Bellingham, highlighting his importance to the team beyond his attacking contributions.

"He is a unique kind of player, extremely important for the team," said Mourinho.

"His mental strength, tactical ability, the way he recovers the ball, the way he pressures, the way he plays up front.

"We like talking about Kylian, Vini [Vinicius Jr] and Jude, but I'm really happy with all the players.

"We have great, great players here."

Mourinho also gave his perspective on the Ballon d'Or debate, arguing that winning the Champions League or World Cup should not automatically make a player the favourite for the individual award.

"It's a very beautiful thing individually and that enters into the individual history of a certain player," Mourinho said.

"I think it's normal that there are a dozen players of a very high level, of which we have three or four. It is normal that it exists as an ambition."

Mourinho suggested the prize should be ultimately measured by a player's lasting impact on the game.

"For me, the Ballon d'Or has to be one of those players that when he finishes playing, we miss for eternity," Mourinho said.

"I miss Maradona, Ronaldinho, Ronaldo, Cristiano, Messi, Zizou, Lothar Matthaus - I miss these people.

"You can't give the Ballon d'Or to a player because he won the Champions League or because he won the World Cup. It doesn't have to be from Paris St-Germain or the Spanish national team."

title: Ipswich sign Argentina World Cup winner Palacios
description: Argentina midfielder Exequiel Palacios becomes the first World Cup winner to sign for Ipswich Town after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.
fullText:
Argentina midfielder Exequiel Palacios has become the first World Cup winner to sign for Ipswich Town after joining from Bayer Leverkusen.

Palacios, 27, left the Bundesliga club for an undisclosed fee and has signed a four-year contract with the Premier League newcomers.

He was part of the Argentina side that both won the World Cup in 2022 and reached the final this summer while he also won the Copa America twice with his country.

"This is a club with great ambition and I am excited to play football in England and compete against some of the best clubs and players in the world," Palacios said.

Palacios, Ipswich's 11th signing of the transfer window, started Argentina's 3-1 win against World Cup debutants Jordan in the group stage in his only appearance at the 2026 tournament.

Ipswich manager Gary O'Neil added: "He is a player who has had real success at the top level of the game, winning the biggest prize of all in the World Cup, as well as major trophies at club level.

"That experience will be vital for us as we continue to work to improve the squad this summer."

Palacios made his senior debut for his boyhood club River Plate in 2015 and won the Copa Libertadores in 2018 and the Copa Argentina twice.

He moved to Germany in 2020 and made 24 appearances as Leverkusen claimed their first-ever Bundesliga title in 2023-24.

Under current Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso, he also won the DFB Pokal and the German Super Cup during his six years at the BayArena.

He departs Leverkusen after making 186 appearances and scoring 15 goals.

Ipswich have spent more than £150m since returning to the Premier League and are also progressing with a move to sign Tammy Abraham on loan from Aston Villa.

They made a winning return to the top flight, defeating Sunderland 2-1 at Portman Road and have also reached the third round of the Carabao Cup at the expense of League One Leicester City.

title: Fan backlash as gay World Cup star joins Saudi club
description: Spain forward Esther Gonzalez attracts backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.
fullText:
Spain forward Esther Gonzalez has attracted backlash after signing for Saudi Women's Premier League side Al Qadsiah.

The 33-year-old agreed a mutual contract termination with National Women's Soccer League champions Gotham FC in July to temporarily step away from the sport to "attend to personal matters in Spain", according to the club's statement.

Gonzalez, whose contract was due to expire in 2027, said on Instagram the decision was "due to strictly personal reasons", adding New York-based Gotham will "always hold a special place in my heart".

However, on Sunday, Al Qadsiah announced the signing of the 2023 World Cup winner, sparking criticism from both Gotham fans over the nature of her departure, and from within the LGBTQ+ community.

Same-sex relationships and sexual activity are illegal in Saudi Arabia.

Fans on social media questioned her motivations and expressed concerns for her safety while Gotham supporters voiced their disappointment over the messaging around her exit and the club missing out on a transfer fee.

According to Spanish outlet El Mundo,, external Gonzalez has deleted all photos of herself with her wife and their first child, born in January, from her social media accounts since signing for Al Qadsiah.

Gonzalez is not the first footballer to encounter negative reactions for moving to Saudi Arabia, with England midfielder Jordan Henderson attracting criticism following his transfer to Saudi Pro League side Al-Ettifaq in 2023.

The move was described as a "slap in the face" by openly gay footballer Jake Daniels, who had received a message of support from Henderson when he came out.

The former Liverpool captain, who had previously shown his support for the LGBTQ+ community by wearing rainbow laces, a One Love armband, and writing messages of solidarity in a matchday programme, left Al-Ettifaq after six months.

Gonzalez won two NWSL titles, an NWSL Challenge Cup, and the Concacaf W Champions Cup in three seasons after moving to the United States from Real Madrid.

Al Qadsiah finished fourth in the Saudi Women's Premier League in 2025-26.

title: Uefa preparing criminal legal action against Infantino
description: Uefa is pursuing criminal proceedings against Fifa president Gianni Infantino over the scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup.
fullText:
Uefa is preparing criminal legal proceedings against Fifa president Gianni Infantino over the now scrapped plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup and its other competitions to private investors.

Documents seen by BBC Sport show an application has been made by European football's governing body requesting access to evidence and documents for use in proceedings in Switzerland against the embattled president himself, who Uefa accuses of "criminal mismanagement".

Uefa also says it is considering pursuing criminal action against other Fifa officials.

Shortly after this summer's World Cup, Infantino proposed creating a new company, Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE), which would have sold off stakes in Fifa's football competitions to private investors.

The plan was scrapped after widespread backlash.

In the application for evidence, Uefa said: "In truth, it was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from Fifa's most valuable assets to the detriment of Fifa, its members, and other parties within the football family," Uefa's application says.

"Infantino pushed the plan through internal Fifa approval only days earlier at a hastily convened meeting where a limited number of Fifa's management officials and employees - some of whom had never heard of the plan - were given mere hours to sign off on an unprecedented multi-billion dollar scheme."

Key figures at Uefa and in European football met today in Monaco ahead of the Champions League draw, where Infantino's status was one item on the agenda.

A statement sent to the media by Uefa said: "Those present unanimously mandated the Uefa president and administration to pursue every available institutional, political and legal avenue necessary to secure fundamental reform, restore proper limits on presidential authority and ensure that Fifa is once again governed as an institution – not around one individual."

BBC Sport has approached Infantino and Fifa for comment.

Uefa also claims that the valuation of the stakes to be sold were not independently verified and would have been offered too cheaply, calling the proposed sale "a fraudulently off-market price promoted by Infantino for his own benefit".

The application adds: "Under the terms Infantino announced, those investors stood to acquire a permanent financial interest in Fifa's commercial arm for $4.2bn, implying an absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn, a figure that was neither the product of an open, competitive auction, nor tested by any independent valuer."

In the application, Uefa is applying to a court in Florida to attempt to access files held by two Fifa businesses - Fifa Americas and FWC2026 - to be used to pursue the criminal charges in Switzerland at a later stage.

The two businesses are based in Florida.

Uefa claims that its 55 member nations would have potentially been harmed by the sell-off plan, and that it may pursue criminal proceedings against other Fifa officials as well as Infantino.

"Uefa and other interested parties are preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other Fifa officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement," the application states.

"The secretive structuring, valuation, financing, and marketing inflicted direct and concrete injury on Fifa's reputation, governance authority, and commercial relationships to the detriment of Fifa as well as its 211 members, including Uefa's 55 member associations."

Uefa insists that the plan was concocted without the knowledge of them or other key stakeholders in football, and that it had been long in development.

The applications says: "On July 28, 2026, without consulting the Fifa Council, Uefa, or any of the other confederations, or any of the 211 Fifa member associations, Infantino, purportedly acting on behalf of Fifa, publicly announced a plan to place the commercial rights to the men's and women's World Cups and the Club World Cup into a new subsidiary: Fifa Forward Enterprise.

"That announcement by Infantino was the public unveiling of a plan that he and a small circle of co-conspirators had conceived and reportedly been developing in secret for more than a year."

Uefa states in the document that there has been "an enduring history of corruption among Fifa officials" and claims that world football's governing body only relents on its plans when pressure comes from outside the sport.

"Fifa's extraordinary power over world football has operated largely without meaningful internal constraint, with accountability coming principally through external forces, including political pressure, public scrutiny, and intervention through international criminal law enforcement," the application adds.

Fifa's headquarters are in the Swiss city of Zurich, and Uefa says that its plan to eventually pursue criminal charges against Infantino is backed up by Swiss law.

"Swiss counsel has confirmed [...] that the proceeding is within reasonable contemplation for purposes of Swiss law and that Uefa has standing, as a complainant, to file a criminal complaint for criminal mismanagement against Infantino and potentially other Fifa officials as may be warranted."

It has been reported that a separate filing has been lodged to a court in New York, where Uefa are seeking documentation from Thrive Capital, the business proposed to take up an interest in FFE which was founded by Josh Kushner, the brother of US president Donald Trump's son-in-law.

Reports indicate there is a third application in Colorado, relating to former Formula 1 chief Greg Maffei, who is referred to in the court filings as a "key commercial adviser" on the proposed FFE transaction.

BBC Sport has also approached Uefa for comment.

Uefa to push to remove Infantino after dropping boycott

Infantino offered Fifa's 211 member associations $40m (£30m) if they backed the proposal for private investment in its tournaments via FFE, including the men's and women's World Cups.

The Swiss has faced calls to step down after he scrapped the controversial plan earlier this month.

Uefa has led the backlash to the proposal, stating it had lost confidence in Infantino, and with its members voting to boycott World Cups unless the FFE plan was scrapped.

Infantino, who is seeking a fourth a term as Fifa president in March, was accused of breaking trust "through deception" in an open letter issued by Uefa, Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation.

The football associations of all the home nations have withdrawn support for Infantino, but he retains the support of South American governing body Conmebol and Caf, the African governing body, while some nations have broken ranks from their confederations to come out in support of the Fifa president.

title: PWR attendances rise by 23% after World Cup
description: Premiership Women's Rugby says average attendances rose by 23.4% during the 2025-26 season, which concluded in June with Saracens winning a record fourth title.
fullText:
Premiership Women's Rugby says average attendances rose by 23.4% during the 2025-26 season, which concluded in June with Saracens winning a record fourth title.

The numbers have been aided by the boost the sport received by England winning a home World Cup at Twickenham in September 2025 and come despite the departure of United States star Ilona Maher from Bristol Bears.

Maher, who is the most followed rugby union player in the world on social media, generated unprecedented attention for the league during her stint in Bristol during the 2024-25 campaign.

The league also reported a 132% increase in social media following, a 310% growth in its database and more than 111 million views across YouTube, Meta and TikTok - a 174% increase in viewing figures.

Last season was the first during which every PWR match was broadcast live across platforms including TNT Sports, BBC Sport and YouTube.

PWR executive chair Genevieve Shore said the figures were encouraging given the high benchmark set by the 2024-25 season.

"Ilona's impact was extraordinary," Shore said. "It brought a huge amount of attention to our league and to our players, and we should absolutely celebrate that.

"So when you look at the fact that we have continued to grow from there, post-World Cup and after that incredible spike in interest, I think that is particularly encouraging.

"We can see growth across so many different areas of the business, and that gives us confidence that the work we're doing is truly connecting with fans."

title: Uefa set to drop Fifa tournament boycott threat
description: Uefa is set to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions, having received assurances there will be no repeat of Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, BBC Sport has been told.
fullText:
Uefa is set to drop its threat of boycotting Fifa competitions, having received assurances there will be no repeat of Gianni Infantino's plan to sell off stakes in the World Cup to private investors, BBC Sport has been told.

Fifa has welcomed the development, saying it is "pleased that all qualified teams will be participating in the upcoming Under-20 Women's World Cup".

The matter will be formally discussed at a meeting of Uefa's executive committee in Monaco on Thursday.

Earlier this month, European football's governing body said that despite Infantino's plan being aborted following widespread condemnation, the conditions required to prevent a boycott had "not been met".

"Assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again," Uefa insisted.

That came after Infantino and Fifa Secretary General Mattias Grafstrom had told national member associations that the FFE proposal was "now off the table", and apologised for "errors".

If the boycott threat is lifted, it will mean next month's Under-20 Women's World Cup will proceed as planned.

Six European teams - England, France, Italy, Portugal, Spain and hosts Poland - are scheduled to play in the tournament.

Uefa has led the backlash against Infantino, and along with Concacaf and the Asian Football Confederation, is expected to continue to push for an overhaul of Fifa's leadership. Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin has said he expects Infantino to resign or to face a challenge to his role from another candidate at elections in March.

A Fifa spokesperson said it "strongly believes that football has the power to unite, even in challenging circumstances" and Fifa "remains committed" to furthering "global development of the game" in "full dialogue with the confederations and stakeholders".

One source close to the discussions insisted this was not a climbdown by Uefa, adding that Infantino's opponents "will continue until there are wholesale changes".

"It is not a Uefa defeat, rather the reality of avoiding hurting young players [over a] once-in-a-lifetime opportunity," they added.

"The actions and insistence on change will continue, and will win out in the end."

Last month, European football's 55 member associations voted to boycott all Fifa competitions until the Fifa Forward Enterprises proposal was dropped "in its entirety and binding assurances have been given that Fifa will never again open its governance or competitions to private ownership".

Uefa has been approached for comment.

Culture secretary Lisa Nandy said this month she would not support a boycott of the U20 World Cup.

"I am not generally in favour of sporting boycotts full stop, because I think they divide people from one another. I think they unfairly penalise athletes and competitors who are not responsible for the reason that these boycotts take place," she said.

"What I would like to see actually is football coming together, resolving this, a change of leadership, a change of direction and a very clear message that football belongs to its fans and it will not have women and girls penalised when the women's game is going from strength to strength. And our Lionesses are leading the world in that."

Will a Premier League club break record for transfer sales in one window?

On Tuesday, a group of former players published a statement saying "change is necessary" at the head of Fifa.

Former Manchester United and France defender Mikael Silvestre, who sits on Fifa's Players' Voice Panel, issued a statement on X on Monday in a post he titled "Enough is Enough!".

The statement has been shared on social media by the likes of England defender Lucy Bronze, France's 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit and former England goalkeeper David James.

However on Wednesday, a different group of former players including World Cup-winning Brazil captain Cafu, former Italy striker Christian Vieri, former Portugal captain Pepe and ex-Argentina international Esteban Cambiasso all posted supportive messages for Infantino on social media.

All of the players are so-called Fifa Legends, officially recognised by the governing body.

Vieri's statement said: "Over the past 10 years, we have seen the work Fifa and President Infantino have done to create representativity for players in football, which did not exist.

"We will remain available to support the great evolution our game has seen this past decade, so that it keeps reaching and benefiting people of every country that plays football all around the world."

This news will come as a major relief to the European Women's U20 players that have been in a degree of limbo over recent weeks, but who will now hope they can prepare to travel to Poland to compete in the forthcoming World Cup.

Meanwhile, Fifa president Infantino may well view it as a significant victory in his increasingly acrimonious battle with Uefa, as he clings to power.

While the nature of the assurances it has received are yet to become clear, despite its tough talk of possible boycotts and legal action, Europe's governing body now runs the risk of being seen to have caved in, having issued what amounted to a hollow threat.

title: England World Cup hopes end after Netherlands draw
description: England's chances of World Cup glory are over after they draw 2-2 with the Netherlands.
fullText:
England's World Cup hopes are over after they drew 2-2 with the Netherlands in their final Pool E game.

Zak Jones' side had to beat the co-hosts to have a chance of progressing from the second pool stage to the semi-finals.

They went ahead after five minutes through Stuart Rushmere, but the Netherlands, three-time World Cup winners, responded through Jip Janssen and Thierry Brinkman.

Henry Croft levelled for England early in the fourth quarter, but they could not find a winner in Amstelveen.

"[I am] gutted, heartbroken. It hurts a lot," said England captain Zach Wallace.

"We gave it everything and we put in a performance we can be proud of. In the end it wasn't to be.

"Some decisions fell against us and some balls didn't fall our way. It's those details at the top level."

The result means the Netherlands top the group and advance to the semi-finals from Pool E along with Argentina, with England third and India in fourth.

Germany and Spain complete the semi-final line-up.

England's final game of the tournament will be the fifth-place match against Australia at the same stadium on Friday (14:00 BST).

title: Maradona's 'Hand of God' ball sells for £2.5m
description: The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal in the 1986 World Cup quarter-final victory over England is sold at auction.
fullText:
The football with which Diego Maradona scored his famous 'hand of God' goal at the 1986 World Cup has sold at auction for £2.5m.

Maradona famously punched the ball past goalkeeper Peter Shilton in Argentina's 2-1 quarter-final win over England.

After the game, he told reporters it had been scored "a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God".

Maradona later scored what became known as the 'goal of the century' in the same game, dribbling past five England outfield players before slotting the ball past Shilton.

Though it sold for $3.3m (£2.5m) at Heritage Auctions in the United States on Saturday, the ball had been expected to fetch nearer $10m (£7.3m).

Speaking to Reuters before the auction, Mike Provenzale, a specialist auctioneer at Heritage, said: "It's a true one-of-one item. Arguably the most significant soccer item that exists."

Tunisian Ali Bin Nasser, who refereed the match in 1986, collected the Adidas Azteca ball at full-time and kept it for more than three decades.

In 2023, he signed a letter to confirm it was the only ball used during the match, which has also been confirmed by further independent authentication.

Bin Nasser sold the ball in 2022 for $2.37m (£1.74m). Its new owner again put it up for auction in 2023 though it did not sell as bids did not meet the minimum value set.

The shirt worn by Maradona during the same match sold for £7.1m at auction in 2022.

title: Infantino must remember he is European - Ceferin
description: Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin says his Fifa counterpart Gianni Infantino's attempt to sell off a stake in the World Cup was "worse than the Super League".
fullText:
Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin says Gianni Infantino needs to remember he is European after describing his Fifa counterpart's plan to sell off a stake in the World Cup as "worse than the Super League".

Earlier this month the world governing body abandoned Infantino's proposal to create a new company - Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) - to manage the commercial and ticketing rights of all Fifa competitions, with 21% to be sold off to a private investment company.

Uefa led opposition to the plan, with its members voting to boycott World Cups unless it was scrapped.

European football's governing body has since said it has lost confidence in Infantino, while the football associations of all the home nations have withdrawn support for the 56-year-old Swiss.

"I think this plan is even worse than the Super League plan," Ceferin told the Rest is Politics podcast., external

"Super important clubs wanted to do their own league, which is wrong, and would destroy football. But in this case, football would be literally sold.

"I'm absolutely sure that the plan is dead. It's hard to to imagine what kind of people would sell the sport that belongs to everyone. We will not allow that to happen."

The European Super League was a proposed breakaway league of 20 top European clubs as a rival to Uefa's Champions League, but the project fell apart days after its unveiling in April 2021 after widespread criticism.

Ceferin said that Uefa had no prior knowledge of Infantino's plan, and that he found out through the media while on holiday with his family.

"He didn't contact me since this happened," Ceferin said.

"They [Fifa] play on, you know, '[how] arrogant Europe is against us: They have enough money, but I help the small and the poor'.

"But I think someone should remind him that he is a European, and that he was supported by Uefa, which he forgot."

Infantino - who worked at Uefa for 16 years, and was general secretary for nine - has been flying around the world in the search of public support.

On Saturday, he met with Caribbean Football Union members in the Dominican Republic and on Sunday he was at the E-Sports World Cup in Paris, attended by the French President Emmanuel Macron, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Portugal forward Cristiano Ronaldo.

Infantino asked to stay away from youth tournament

Scottish FA withdraws support for Fifa president Infantino

Ceferin confirmed he would not run to become Fifa president at the Fifa Congress in March 2027, when Infantino will look to secure a fourth term in the role.

"I'm not interested because of two reasons. One reason is that I love Uefa and I love working here, and I think that at a certain point it's time also to enjoy life a bit," the 58-year-old Slovenian said.

"And the second point is, my credibility is much, much, much higher if I'm not interested in the position."

Before his aborted FFE proposal, Infantino was coming under increasing pressure over his relationship with United States President Donald Trump.

After US striker Folarin Balogun had a red card suspension overturned so that he could play in his side's defeat by Belgium in the last 16 of this summer's World Cup, Trump revealed he personally called Infantino to request the sanction be lifted.

Earlier this month, Trump said it would be a "terrible mistake" to remove Infantino as Fifa president.

"That was more than shocking. We have rules, and if you don't respect your own rules, then the game doesn't make any sense," Ceferin said on the incident.

"The president of a country says: 'I called him, and I told him to look at it.' And then the Fifa president says it was an independent decision.

"I mean, for us as football fans, or for us as a governing body, that's shocking. That's shocking, and - trust me - almost everybody was shocked. Just not everybody dared to speak."
